h: Miniature railways, canals and Surrey heathland
p: Admiralty Way is just a short drive from Camberley town centre, so it's easy to pair a bounce with a wander around The Atrium and The Square, where there are shops, restaurants and a cinema. If you've got siblings with very different interests, splitting the afternoon between AirHop and town works nicely, and nobody gets bored.

For something a bit special, Frimley Lodge Park, just down the road, is home to a miniature railway that runs on selected days, with little trains puffing around the park. There's also a big play area, open spaces and the Basingstoke Canal running alongside for towpath walks. It's a gentle, outdoorsy contrast to a hectic hour on the trampolines.

Lightwater Country Park, a short drive north, has heathland, woodland trails and ponds to explore, with a visitor centre and play area too. Swinley Forest near Bracknell is popular with families for walks, cycle trails and outdoor adventures among the pines. Camberley also has a long military connection, with the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst just on the edge of town, where officers of the British Army are trained. A couple of tips for AirHop itself: if you've got younger children, look out for sessions aimed at them, which can be calmer than busy weekend afternoons. Bring a drink and a snack for afterwards, and wear clothes that are comfortable for jumping, as you'll be bouncing for a good while. The Basingstoke Canal towpath is also a great way to stretch the legs afterwards, with narrowboats, ducks and peaceful water to slow everyone down before the drive home.
